setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

starting_state: A new empty project, stopped, with Record off. No pattern has trigs, and no trig algorithm has been chosen yet. The first step opens the Pattern editor and picks the algorithm.

steps.caption: In a new empty project with playback stopped and Record off, tap Pattern (5,8), then tap the third algorithm button (14,2). The five algorithm buttons on row 2 are, from the left: Drum (12,2), a library of classic bass, snare and hi-hat patterns; Tresillo (13,2), a 3-3-2 grouping; Euclidean (14,2), trigs spread as evenly as a mathematical rule allows; Numeric (15,2), patterns from Noise Engineering's Numeric Repetitor; and Rhythm Doctor (16,2). The Trig Algorithm screen marks Euclidean as SELECTED and the fader on grid row 2 lights its third position.
steps.title: Choose Euclidean

steps.caption: Turn E2 left. The screen passes Tresillo and stops on Drum, the first algorithm (a further turn stays on Drum). Drum shows no SELECTED mark and the third fader position stays lit: turning E2 only browses. Euclidean is still the algorithm in use until you press K3.
steps.title: Browse without applying

steps.caption: Press K3. Drum now reads SELECTED and the fader lights its first position. Drum draws on classic drum patterns, so it suits a kick, snare or hi-hat lane, where Euclidean suits an even pulse.
steps.title: Apply Drum

steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8). The Paint Preview screen opens on Algorithm Drum with Shift 0, but no step flashes on the pattern grid: at its default settings Drum previews no steps. Prime previews whichever algorithm is selected.
steps.title: Prime with Drum selected

steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8). The preview closes and nothing was painted.
steps.title: Cancel the empty preview

steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Pattern tasks, turn E2 to Algorithm and press K3. The Trig Algorithm screen returns (a Painting cancelled tip may still show) and Drum is still SELECTED.
steps.title: Return to the algorithm list

steps.caption: Turn E2 two detents right, past Tresillo. Euclidean is highlighted but carries no SELECTED mark yet, and the fader still shows Drum.
steps.title: Browse back to Euclidean

steps.caption: Press K3. Euclidean reads SELECTED and the fader lights its third position again.
steps.title: Apply Euclidean

steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8) again. Now every step on the pattern grid flashes and Paint Preview reads 64 trigs: at the default settings Euclidean fills all 64 steps, where Drum previewed none. Prime always previews the algorithm that is selected, so changing the algorithm changes what Prime shows.
steps.title: Prime now previews Euclidean

steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8) to close the Euclidean preview and tap Tresillo (13,2), the second algorithm button. Like Drum, Tresillo previews nothing until you choose a pattern: tap drum bank 1 at (12,3), then tap both ends of the first fader on row 2, (2,2) and (10,2), and of the second fader on row 3, (2,3) and (10,3). Tap Prime (16,8). The algorithm fader lights its second position and Paint Preview reads Algorithm Tresillo with 8 trigs. The flashing steps are spaced 9, 9 and 6 steps apart, over and over: the 3-3-2 grouping, scaled up. Nothing is painted yet.
steps.title: Prime Tresillo for a 3-3-2 preview

title: Choose a trig algorithm
